reason: Measured all three instances in Chromium with per-line client rects at 320/390/768/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440, then re-measured with pretty forced back and with the proposed nbsp binder applied verbatim. One sub-instance is real; the finding around it is wrong on mechanism, wrong on geometry, wrong on its numbers, and its fix is a measured net regression that also collides on paper. (1) MECHANISM IS FALSE FOR INSTANCE 2. .b-unit has no text-wrap declaration at all - computed text-wrap is 'wrap', not 'balance' (b.css:76-83; the only later rule touching it, b.css:1384, sets text-transform/letter-spacing/colour). The print dateline's three-line stack is flex shrink inside a 220px print column, not balance choosing a joint. The finding's headline - 'Every generated sentence is handed to text-wrap: balance ... which repeatedly makes it choose the worst joint' - is untrue of a third of its own evidence. (2) THE PRINT GEOMETRY IS INVERTED, AND THE FIX WOULD BREAK THE KEEPSAKE. At 1440 the dateline box measures left 550, right 635; .b-two's second column (.b-measure, the rail and the DAYS AWAY head) begins at x=640. That is 5px of clearance, not 'roughly 100px of free paper to its right' - the span already overflows its own 220px column by 34px. Widening it from 84px to 152px puts its right edge at ~702, i.e. 62px inside the rail column, under the head and across the count lane. Screenshot-verified. That is 'the fix would make the work worse', on the one artifact that cannot be reloaded and corrected. (3) NUMBERS ARE WRONG. Breaking after 'April.' measures 199/274, not 212/262 (measured against the live computed font and letterfit). The conclusion survives; the arithmetic offered as proof does not. (4) 'IDENTICAL AT 390/768/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440' IS FALSE. The print unit sets two lines at 390 ('days away on Thursday' / '16 July 2026'), ONE line at 768, and three only at 1024 and above. (5) THE FIX, APPLIED VERBATIM, DOES NOT DO WHAT IS CLAIMED. With the exact 26-word list run over the six selectors: .b-behindNote is fixed (227/247 -> 254/219, 'The city' held together) - the one genuine win. .b-unit print is NOT fixed - it still sets three lines ('days away' / 'on Thursday' / '16 July 2026'); only the 152px collision would fix it. .b-emptyBody merely moves the break from after 'from' to after 'it,' - and 'it,' carries a comma, so it escapes the closed list, meaning the finding's own proposed assertion ('no rendered line ends on a word from that list') PASSES on a line that still ends on a stranded pronoun. A gate that green-lights the defect it was written to catch is not a gate. (6) IT PARTLY UNDOES THE ROUND-7 FIX IT CITES AS PRECEDENT. Rag after the binder: .b-pressBody 357/344 (13px) -> 325/376 (51px); .b-emptyBody 312/295 (17px) -> 329/278 (51px). Chained binds create long unbreakable runs ('it~is~the~only', 'and~the~plan,'); at a 280px measure .b-emptyBody goes from two lines to three. (7) BALANCE IS NOT WORSE THAN PRETTY HERE, WHICH IS THE FINDING'S PREMISE. Forced back to pretty, .b-behindNote sets 349/125 at 390 and 292/182 at 768 - the confirmed round-7 ragging defect, restored - and pretty strands function words too: .b-emptyBody ends line 1 on 'is', .b-pressBody at 768 ends line 1 on 'no', splitting 'no notes'. Balance trades one imperfection for a strictly smaller one; no regression is established. (8) MAINTAINABILITY, AS ASKED. 152px is hand-tuned to the single string 'Thursday 16 July 2026'; a Wednesday or a September re-breaks it, and the number is off the ladder. The word-list binder is content-independent but its output under balance is a Chromium line-breaker outcome, so the proposed assertion is version- and metrics-sensitive - it would flap. What survives all of this is one stranded article in one sentence on one surface: worth a line of polish, not a systemic finding, and nowhere near the 9.5 bar as filed.
sharpenedFix: If the panel wants the one real instance closed, do it narrowly and without touching the other five selectors. Bind ONLY a sentence-opening article - i.e. replace the space after a capitalised The/A/An that immediately follows '. ' - inside the guest behind-note sentence built at render-b.js:335-339. That is a single joint, it does not chain, and it leaves .b-pressBody, .b-emptyBody, .b-endedBody and .b-gapNote rags exactly where round 7 put them (measured: .b-behindNote 227/247 -> 254/219; every other selector unchanged). Cheaper still, and probably better: the sentence itself is the problem - 'The Orchard reserved, 18 April. The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead.' repeats 'The' as the first word of both clauses. Dropping the second article ('City hotel shortlist is not going ahead.') or recasting it removes the joint rather than welding it. Leave .b-unit alone: its three-line set is a flex-shrink question inside a 220px print column with 5px of clearance to the rail, and any fix there is a print-column geometry change that must be measured against x=640, not a text-wrap change.
